answer: Harrison Community Hospital (HCH) is a 25-bed Critical Access Hospital in Cadiz, Ohio, serving Harrison County and the surrounding tri-state region for more than 50 years. The 340B Drug Pricing Program enables HCH to maximize limited resources and reinvest savings into programs and services that support low-income, uninsured, underinsured, homeless, and rural patients. HCH offers a broad range of healthcare services, including: 24-hour emergency care, surgical services, diagnostic imaging, inpatient and outpatient laboratory services, rehabilitation and therapy services, swing bed care, outpatient infusion services and primary care.

In 2024, 340B savings offset 17.9% of Harrison Community Hospital's total charity care, uncompensated care, and bad debt expense. While these savings are critical to sustaining access to care, the hospital continues to absorb most of these costs as part of its mission to serve all patients, regardless of their ability to pay. While 340B savings support these efforts, the hospital continues to provide significant levels of charity and uncompensated care beyond the resources generated through the program. These investments reflect HCH's ongoing commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves through quality care, expanded access to services, and support for healthcare workforce development.
340B program savings are reinvested in three key areas:
Charity Care – Providing financial assistance to patients who are unable to afford healthcare services.
Facility Improvements – Maintaining and upgrading facilities and equipment to support a safe, high-quality care environment.
Service Preservation – Sustaining essential healthcare services locally, reducing the need for uninsured and underserved patients to travel long distances for care.
